question: A team has spent three weeks refining a Claude-assisted weekly digest. The last two rounds of changes produced no difference anyone could notice. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: A) Ask Claude to grade its own digests and continue until the grades stop rising
B) Keep refining until the digest needs no editing at all before it is circulated
C) Start again with a fresh set of instructions written by a different team member
D) Put the current version into use and review it after a period of real work
correct_answers: D) Put the current version into use and review it after a period of real work
explanations: Self-grading tells the team how the digest scores itself, which is not the same as whether readers can use it.
Requiring zero editing sets a standard the arrangement was never designed to meet and delays any benefit indefinitely.
Discarding three weeks of refinement resets the work without any evidence that a fresh start would do better.
Correct. Iteration has stopped yielding gains, so the remaining information will come from real use. Adopting it with a review date set keeps the loop open without spending more effort on a plateau.
